I've been farming this land for 40 years and I know this Quzhou soil well. My 4.5 mu is all double-cropped — wheat goes in after maize harvest in October, maize follows after wheat harvest in June. Same land, both crops, every year. My household is small now, my son works in the city, so it's mostly me. I rely on mechanized operations and the village cooperative for seeding and harvesting. I can't afford to cut corners on inputs because yield is everything on 4.5 mu — but I also can't waste money on excess fertilizer, the government inspectors have been watching nitrogen use.

**Wheat:** I'll plant all 4.5 mu with Jimai 22 — it's a high-yield, disease-resistant improved variety I've trusted for years. I'll do rotary tillage after maize harvest to incorporate the straw, which saves me buying extra organic matter. I'll apply base fertilizer before seeding: compound fertilizer plus urea topdress at jointing in March. Three irrigations — freeze water in late November, jointing water in April, grain filling water in May. I know from experience that skipping the freeze water is a gamble I'm not willing to take. Two pesticide passes: herbicide in winter, aphid/rust control in late April.

**Maize:** Right after wheat harvest I'll go no-till and direct-seed hybrid Xianyu 335 into the stubble — saves time and moisture. I'll apply compound fertilizer at seeding and topdress nitrogen at the big bell stage. Two irrigations only — one at emergence if July is dry, one at tasseling. Summer rains usually help. Two pesticide passes: herbicide and corn borer control.
